correctness.rationale: The deletion-output equivalence is exactly pairwise block-equality preservation. Shift-invariance forces the interval names into a least-period d sequence of d different blocks; outside-element comparison forces complete isolation unless d=1. Contracting the constant interval contributes S(n-l+1,k), and isolating d internal residue-class blocks contributes S(n-l,k-d) for each d>=2. Summing proves the Bell formula and all-length bounds. Standalone brute force passed 899301 pair comparisons through length 9, Stirling totals at all tested lengths, and 11800 larger seeded checks. A standard Bell-ratio estimate supports the stated asymptotics; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The unlabeled-block deletion observation is a natural model in symbolic clustering and partition-valued reads. Unlike elementary labeled-word deletion runs, it admits nonlocal equal outputs governed by a precise isolated-periodic structure. The exact formulas refine collisions simultaneously by distance and block richness for all n, and show that exceptional nonlocal redundancy is asymptotically negligible in a uniform random partition. This structural distinction is meaningful without claiming optimal code sizes.
